subtitulo: When to link and when to let silence link
descripcion: At C2 discourse markers are used sparingly enough that their absence becomes part of the style: a writer capable of dense linking can choose bare juxtaposition instead, trusting the logical connection to be self-evident, which reads as more confident than marking every step.

filas: However, despite this, and as a result, the plan failed.
The warnings went unheeded. The plan failed.
when the logical link is genuinely obvious

ejemplos.texto: The warnings went unheeded. The plan failed.
He said nothing. That, in itself, was the answer.
The numbers were revised. Nobody was surprised.

notas: Bare juxtaposition works only when the causal or logical link is genuinely obvious to the reader without a marker — forcing it where the link isn't clear creates confusion, not sophistication.
A writer who can produce dense, fully marked prose and chooses not to reads as more confident than one who never marks anything, because the omission is legible as a choice.
Mixing marked and bare sentences within a passage, using bare ones for the strongest logical steps, is itself a rhetorical technique.

es.en: Formal Spanish has a rich set of connectors («por consiguiente, no obstante, asimismo»), and translating each one (consequently, nevertheless, likewise) produces over-linked English. Polished English often drops the connector and lets the logic speak for itself.
es.es: El español formal dispone de un amplio repertorio de conectores («por consiguiente», «no obstante», «asimismo»), y traducirlos todos como «consequently», «nevertheless», «likewise» produce un inglés excesivamente enlazado. El inglés pulido suele omitir el conector y dejar que la lógica se entienda sola.

de.en: Formal German uses many connectors («zudem, allerdings, somit»), and translating each one produces over-linked English. The German word «also» is a false friend: it means so or therefore, not also.
de.de: Formelles Deutsch verwendet viele Konnektoren («zudem, allerdings, somit»), und wenn jeder davon übersetzt wird, wirkt das Englische überverknüpft. Das deutsche «also» ist zudem ein falscher Freund: Es bedeutet «so» oder «therefore», nicht «also».

it.en: Formal Italian uses many connectors («inoltre, tuttavia, pertanto»), and translating each one produces over-linked English. Polished English often drops the connector altogether.
it.it: L'italiano formale usa molti connettivi («inoltre», «tuttavia», «pertanto»), e tradurli tutti produce un inglese eccessivamente connesso. L'inglese elegante spesso elimina del tutto il connettivo.

fr.en: Formal French uses many connectors («en outre, toutefois, par conséquent»), and «en effet» is a false friend: it means indeed or because, not in effect. Polished English often drops the connector altogether.
fr.fr: Le français formel utilise beaucoup de connecteurs («en outre», «toutefois», «par conséquent»), et «en effet» est un faux ami : il signifie «indeed» ou parfois «because», pas «in effect». L'anglais soigné omet souvent complètement le connecteur.

pt.en: Formal Portuguese uses many connectors («além disso, contudo, portanto»), and «aliás» is a false friend: it means besides or actually, not alias. Polished English often drops the connector altogether.
pt.pt: O português formal usa muitos conectores («além disso», «contudo», «portanto»), e «aliás» é um falso amigo: significa «besides» ou «actually», não «alias». O inglês bem lapidado muitas vezes elimina o conector por completo.

errores: Using bare juxtaposition where the logical link genuinely isn't obvious, leaving the reader confused.
Never marking anything, which reads as underdeveloped rather than confident.
Marking every single step so densely that the prose loses all rhythm.

es: «*es decir*» rendered as *it is to say* instead of *that is* or *in other words*.
de: «*das heisst*» rendered as *that is called* instead of *that is* or *in other words*.
it: «*vale a dire*» rendered as *it's worth saying* instead of *that is to say*.
fr: «*c'est-à-dire*» rendered as *it is to say* instead of *that is* or *in other words*.
pt: «*quer dizer*» rendered as *it wants to say* instead of *I mean* or *that is*.

redemittel.expresion: That, in itself, was the answer.

traducciones.es: Eso, en sí mismo, fue la respuesta.
traducciones.de: Das war an sich schon die Antwort.
traducciones.it: Quella, di per sé, era la risposta.
traducciones.pt: Isso, por si só, era a resposta.

redemittel.funcion: explicit marker for a genuine causal chain

redemittel.expresion: The two facts sit side by side.
redemittel.funcion: names juxtaposition as a deliberate choice

traducciones.es: Los dos hechos quedan uno al lado del otro.
traducciones.fr: Les deux faits se tiennent côte à côte.
traducciones.it: I due fatti stanno l'uno accanto all'altro.
traducciones.pt: Os dois factos ficam lado a lado.

redemittel.funcion: denies an inference the reader might draw

traducciones.es: No es que se siga de ahí.

redemittel.expresion: Whether the two are connected is another matter.

traducciones.es: Si ambas cosas están conectadas es otro asunto.
traducciones.de: Ob beides zusammenhängt, ist eine andere Frage.
traducciones.fr: Savoir si les deux sont liés est une autre affaire.
traducciones.it: Se le due cose siano collegate è un'altra questione.
traducciones.pt: Se as duas coisas estão ligadas é outra questão.

redemittel.expresion: Every marker here would be one too many.

traducciones.es: Acá cualquier conector sería uno de más.
traducciones.de: Jeder Konnektor wäre hier einer zu viel.
traducciones.fr: Ici, chaque connecteur serait un de trop.
traducciones.it: Qui ogni connettivo sarebbe uno di troppo.
traducciones.pt: Aqui qualquer conector seria um a mais.

mision.consigna: Write a reflective piece about the mental load in a relationship.
requisitos: markers only where their absence would confuse

microtareas.texto: Write about *being taken advantage of* in five sentences with no connectors.
Add one marker. Does it help or explain too much?
Record 2 minutes on *harbouring resentment*; notice your habitual *and so*.

autochequeo: Is bare juxtaposition used only where the link is genuinely obvious?
Does the passage mix marked and bare sentences deliberately, not randomly?
Would a reader follow the logic without confusion where markers are dropped?
Is at least one strong logical step left bare, for effect?
Does the prose have rhythm, not either constant marking or none at all?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on the choice between marked linking and bare juxtaposition. Check whether every bare link is genuinely self-evident. Do not rewrite the text.
